substillus , a, um, adj. sub - stillo (ante- and post - class.),
I.slightly dropping, dribbling.
I. Adj.: “lotium,” i. e. strangury, Cato, R. R. 156, 6 .—
II. Subst.: substil-lum , i, n., a slight dropping, a sprinkling: “substillum tempus ante pluviam jam paene uvidum et post pluviam non persiccum, quod jam stillaret, aut nondum desisset, Fest. pp. 306 and 307 Müll.: dehinc substillum et denuo sudum,” Tert. Pall. 2 .
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
